properties.line: New York and Erie: New York/Jersey City – Buffalo

segments.note: Built in stages from an 1841 start (Piermont-Goshen), reaching Middletown by 1843, Port Jervis by 1848, and Binghamton in 1849; completed the full 448-mile mainline to Dunkirk, NY (on Lake Erie, passing through Salamanca) on May 19, 1851 - briefly the longest railroad in the nation. The first through train carried President Millard Fillmore and Secretary of State Daniel Webster, who rode a rocking chair lashed to a flatcar for the view. The original NYC-area terminus was Piermont on the Hudson (reached by ferry from Manhattan); direct Jersey City rail access followed in subsequent years, and the line was later extended from the Dunkirk area to Buffalo as well. Reorganized as the Erie Railway after an 1861 bankruptcy. Frequency estimated, unsourced. Between Deposit and Binghamton the line dips through northeastern Pennsylvania via Lackawaxen and Susquehanna, crossing the Starrucca Viaduct at Lanesboro, PA (completed 1848) - an 1,100-foot stone arch bridge over Starrucca Creek, one of the era's great engineering feats and still in use by rail today.

segments.note: Reorganized as the New York, Lake Erie and Western Railroad in 1878, renamed Erie Railroad in 1895. This was the Erie's own trunk line across the Southern Tier of New York - Salamanca was a major junction where the ex-Atlantic & Great Western route toward Jamestown, Meadville, and Ohio branched off (see atlantic_great_western_jamestown.geojson). The Erie ceased to exist on October 17 1960, merging with the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western to form the Erie Lackawanna - the post-merger years are drawn as erie-mainline-jerseycity-buffalo-el. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

properties.geometry_quality: EASTERN-TERMINAL ERA MISMATCH (pre-existing, not introduced by the 1960 split). The line is drawn to the Erie's Pavonia Terminal in Jersey City, but the Erie began moving its passenger trains out of Pavonia to the Lackawanna's Hoboken Terminal in October 1956, and Pavonia closed in 1958. Erie Lackawanna consolidated all passenger trains at Hoboken. In 1963 EL also abandoned the Erie Main Line south of Paterson through Passaic, rerouting trains onto the ex-Lackawanna Boonton Branch via the Lyndhurst Draw. So for roughly the last 10 miles the drawn alignment is right for the 19th and early 20th century and wrong for the 1956-1970 years: EL passenger trains did not run into Jersey City, and after 1963 did not run through Passaic. The correct post-1963 geometry lies on the ex-Lackawanna route, which is a different feature, so this is documented rather than redrawn. Everything from Suffern west - Port Jervis, Binghamton, Hornell, Salamanca, Buffalo - is unaffected.

segments.note: Erie Lackawanna from the merger of October 17 1960; reorganized as the Erie Lackawanna Railway in 1968 under the Dereco holding company. EL first rerouted its through trains onto the ex-Lackawanna line between Hoboken and Binghamton, then put the Erie-Lackawanna Limited back on this ex-Erie route on October 28 1962. Service was cut back through the decade - by 1963 sleepers ran only Chicago-Binghamton, later only to Hornell - and through passenger service ended with the Lake Cities' final run in January 1970, a year before Amtrak existed. Frequency estimated, unsourced; 240 minutes reflects a service in steep decline, not a timetable.

metadata.note: GEOMETRY UPGRADED 2026-08-23: replaced the original 19-point hand-placed approximation with real-traced OpenStreetMap track geometry (Overpass API, shortest-path graph search) -- still active Norfolk Southern 'Southern Tier' freight trackage today. Traced length 785.5 km / 488.1 mi, Jersey City to Buffalo (the original 1841-51 line ran the shorter Piermont-Dunkirk routing, 448 mi; both endpoints were later extended). See erie_railroad_extensions.geojson for the Chicago extension (via Marion, OH) and the acquired New York, Susquehanna and Western system, and atlantic_great_western_jamestown.geojson for the Salamanca-Jamestown-Meadville-Akron-Dayton broad-gauge extension.
metadata.rule4_split_2026_08_24: Rule 4 ownership split. The Erie Railroad and the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western did not become one another -- they merged on October 17 1960 into a new company, the Erie Lackawanna Railroad (reorganized as the Erie Lackawanna Railway in 1968 under the Dereco holding company, and folded into Conrail April 1 1976). Before this pass the post-1960 years were still drawn in the predecessors' own colours, so one company appeared on the map in two different colours -- ex-Erie segments in Erie black #22223B, ex-Lackawanna in DL&W brown #7F5539. Every feature whose segments ran past 1960 has been split at the merger date into a second feature with identical geometry, company 'Erie Lackawanna Railroad', colour #A02C5A. Six features across six files: erie-mainline-jerseycity-buffalo, dlw-hoboken-scranton-buffalo, erie-salamanca-jamestown-dayton, erie-chicago-extension, erie-buffalo-niagara-falls, cmv-cleveland-youngstown. The NYS&W (nysw-jerseycity-stroudsburg) is deliberately NOT included -- it had reverted to independent operation by 1940 and was not part of the merger.

Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
